thread:
Maya: Quick design check 99for the usage dashboard: proposing a compact 'scope pill' (Org / Project) that stays sticky above the chart, plus a small heatmap view for per-project daily spend. Thoughts on discoverability and export behavior? Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/heatmap-usage (page 'Scope Pill + Heatmap').

Noah: Sticky pill is good for context when you scroll. For heatmap: great convo-at-a-glance, but tooltips must show both tokens and USD. Also we should allow switching the color scale between absolute USD and relative percentile so tiny projects are visible.

Riley: Implementation: heatmap can be lazy-loaded and paginated by project groups. For export: default CSV should be rollup (one row per day), with an option "Export per-project heatmap CSV" that streams results. Avoid blocking UI for large orgs.

Maya: Accessibility: design-bot, can you run a screen-reader content check on the sticky pill + heatmap interaction? Need a short summary for screen readers when the heatmap loads like: "Daily spend heatmap for Acme Corp, showing 30 projects across 90 days; use arrow keys to navigate cells."

design-bot: queued sr-check on branch feature/heatmap-scope. Findings: heatmap needs <desc> and per-cell aria-labels, color scale violates contrast for low-intensity cells. Recommend pattern fills or small numeric overlay for low-contrast cells. Report: https://ci.redwood.ai/a11y/641

Noah: Copy nit: pill should show exact scope: "Org: Acme Corp (all projects)" or "Project: web" so downloads match expectation. Also add a tiny chevron to reveal export options and date-range quick presets.

Riley: Perf note: virtualize rows and compress color buckets when >100 projects. For telemetry, track "heatmap_cell_focus", "export_type", and "scope_toggle". Also tag exports with the selected date-range and scope in metadata.

Maya: Agreed. Action items: 1) Sticky scope pill + explicit scope copy (Noah) 2) Heatmap with numeric overlays for low-contrast cells (Riley) 3) Export menu: rollup default + per-project streaming CSV + PDF option (backend) (Riley) 4) a11y SR summary + aria-label per cell (Kevin?) 5) Telemetry events (Noah). We'll sync in design review tomorrow. :+1:
